//: Composite indexes. Firestore REFUSES any query that filters on one field
and orders by another unless a matching composite index exists — it fails
with FAILED_PRECONDITION rather than degrading to a slow scan. Postgres
simply planned around it, so nothing in the app hinted this was needed.
Every entry below corresponds to a real query in the codebase. Field order
matters: equality filters first (in any order among themselves), then the
orderBy field last. An index whose fields are in the wrong order does not
Deploy with: npx firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes
Building them takes a few minutes on an empty database; queries fail until
previews has no entry on purpose: useGlbPreview queries it with
equalities only (conversation_id, mesh_id, status) and picks the newest
row client-side, because equality-only queries need no composite index.

indexes.//: HistoryView, Sidebar: user's conversations, newest first
messageService, ShareView, HistoryView: a conversation's messages in order
HistoryView first_message lookup also reads descending in places
VisualCard: latest assistant message in a conversation
mesh.ts getPriorImageCallId: conversation-wide latest successful image
mesh.ts: same shape but narrowed by an id list (.in on id)
mesh.ts: newest successful mesh for a user's conversation
